title: Discovery of a magnetic monopole

concept.text: The innovation would be the reproducible discovery of a free particle carrying nonzero magnetic charge: an isolated source of magnetic field whose charge is a measurable particle property. Under the Dirac quantization condition used to define this target, that magnetic charge would be a nonzero integer multiple of the Dirac unit. Establishing the charge is central to the discovery; observing an unusual particle signal alone would leave the defining property unproven.

The target encompasses more than one theoretical possibility. Conventional grand-unified-theory monopoles could be extraordinarily massive, while other scenarios motivate searches at collider-accessible masses. Discovering magnetic charge would therefore open an experimental investigation of the particle's origin, mass, interactions and underlying theory. It would not, by itself, establish that the particle came from grand unification.

significance.text: A confirmed free monopole would establish magnetic charge as an observed particle property and give experimental substance to a longstanding extension of electromagnetism. Adding magnetic sources would make Maxwell's equations more symmetric between electricity and magnetism. Dirac's argument connects the existence of a monopole to the discreteness of electric charge, so discovery would provide a direct experimental handle on charge quantization. Measuring the minimum magnetic charge could also constrain the structure of the underlying gauge group.

These consequences would be fundamental even before a particular theory was identified. Monopoles occur in several theoretical settings, so a discovery would give theories containing them a concrete experimental target without uniquely selecting a grand-unified theory. Establishing the particle's theoretical origin would require additional measurements and comparison with competing predictions.

Some heavy grand-unified monopoles are predicted to catalyze nucleon decay through the Rubakov–Callan effect. Demonstrating that process would be a further discovery, with its own interaction and rate measurements; generic magnetic charge does not establish catalysis. Industrial uses remain speculative in this record, with no demonstrated application or justified practical forecast. Neither catalysis nor an application is required for the fundamental discovery to matter.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a convincing positive measurement of a free particle's magnetic charge, together with reproducibility and adequate rejection of instrumental and particle backgrounds. The documented searches demonstrate ways to look for monopoles and constrain particular possibilities, but they do not supply that discovery measurement. This selected evidence also cannot establish the outcome of every monopole search through 1 November 2026.

Producing or encountering a monopole is a major physical barrier. The IceCube material describes conventional GUT-scale masses above 10^14 GeV, far beyond the reach of the collider scenario considered here. Masses and cosmic abundances depend on the theory and cosmological history; extreme rarity is not a universal prediction established by these sources. Collider searches face limits from available production energy, uncertain production rates and detector acceptance. Cosmic searches instead depend on the incoming flux and on the velocities and interactions to which the detector is sensitive.

The measurement problem is equally important. A trapping search needs a monopole to stop in material that can subsequently be scanned, and the induction detector must distinguish a stable magnetic-charge response from spurious current changes. A track-based search needs enough information, including independently constrained velocity, to distinguish magnetic charge from electrically charged backgrounds. Searches based on monopole-induced nucleon decay also depend on the assumed catalysis cross section; their sensitivity does not transfer automatically to monopoles lacking that interaction.

current_state.text: MoEDAL's 2024 search examined the CMS beam pipe for monopoles produced through the Schwinger effect and trapped in its material. It observed no monopole signal and reported 95% confidence-level exclusions reaching masses of 80 GeV, with its strongest comparative constraints covering magnetic charges from 2 to 45 Dirac units. These are exclusions within the paper's production and trapping assumptions, rather than a model-independent exclusion of every monopole in that mass and charge range. The supplied review reports complete text extraction of the seven-page paper. The research metadata gives 15 August 2024 as the journal publication date, but that exact date was not verified in the reviewed document contents.

The MoEDAL experiment also documents a concrete magnetic-charge measurement method: a trapped monopole passing through a superconducting induction detector would produce a persistent current proportional to its magnetic charge. Calibration and repeated scans are essential because spurious signals can occur, whereas a monopole should give a consistent response. This establishes an experimental route to the target observable, not a positive monopole detection.

The IceCube proceedings supplied as arXiv:2507.05896, dated 8 July 2025 in the research metadata, quote existing slow-monopole flux bounds of approximately 10^-17 to 10^-18 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 at 90% confidence. Those bounds come from a previous analysis and depend on the assumed proton-decay catalysis cross section. The new analysis described in the proceedings was still under development, including training and development of its final event-selection stage; its projected sensitivity must therefore remain separate from completed exclusion results. Although the landing-page evidence was partial, the supplied review also used a complete eleven-page text extraction. No additional numerical result is inferred here from figures that the review did not inspect.

The supplied research additionally attributes limits for charges up to 10 Dirac units to MoEDAL's full-detector Run 2 paper and gives 20 February 2025 as its publication date. However, no document artifact for that citation was retained, so the supplied review could not verify its contents, detailed assumptions or exact date. The reported result remains an unverified part of this account; the access limitation does not establish that it is false.

Evidence limitation: the supplied research also reports a 2025 NOvA null search, but provides no corresponding source, so its scope and numerical results cannot be established here. More broadly, the supplied material contains no search record establishing comprehensive coverage through 1 November 2026. The documented results support specific null searches and an ongoing analysis; they do not justify a definitive statement about every experiment's discovery status at that date.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed completion criterion: reproducibly detect a free particle with nonzero magnetic charge consistent, within measured uncertainty, with a nonzero integer multiple of the Dirac unit. This is a proposed definition for this innovation, not a published consensus standard. The result should measure the defining magnetic charge and quantify its uncertainty, rather than infer a monopole solely from missing energy or an excess of highly ionizing tracks.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed completion criterion

completion_criteria.text: One technically grounded route would be a trapped candidate producing a calibrated persistent-current response in a superconducting induction detector. Repeated scans should return the same magnetic-charge value, with calibration, instrumental artifacts and spurious responses addressed. The relevant observable is the persistent current proportional to magnetic charge; an ordinary trapped superconducting flux quantum alone would not meet this criterion.
completion_criteria.label: One technically grounded route would be a trapped

completion_criteria.text: Proposed alternative route: a particle track with independently constrained velocity and a sufficiently informative detector response to measure magnetic charge and distinguish it from electrically charged backgrounds. Strong ionization would be useful evidence, but would need the additional information that makes the magnetic-charge interpretation discriminating. Reproducibility could involve repeated measurements of a trapped particle, additional consistent events, independent apparatus, or a combination appropriate to the detection method.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed alternative route

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: a convincing discovery report should specify the demonstrated charge range, mass information, velocity range, detector acceptance, interaction assumptions and remaining alternatives. Independent confirmation would strengthen the conclusion. Finite tests would establish the discovery and its measured properties within those conditions; they would not establish every possible monopole species, a unique grand-unified origin, nucleon-decay catalysis or practical utility.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: PHY-07, Observation of baryon-number violation, has a direct theoretical connection through monopole-induced nucleon decay. Some GUT monopoles are predicted to catalyze that process, but measuring magnetic charge would not demonstrate baryon-number violation. Conversely, observing baryon-number violation would not by itself identify a monopole. The two entries therefore retain distinct discovery requirements.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-04, Laboratory identification of the dark-matter particle, and PHY-12, Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale, share the broader goal of identifying new microscopic physics. A monopole discovery would establish neither a dark-matter identity nor an explanation of the Higgs-mass scale without additional evidence. PHY-08, Observation of lepton-number violation, and PHY-13, A tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess, likewise require their own symmetry-violation or cosmological demonstrations; none follows automatically from magnetic charge.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-01, Ambient-pressure superconducting conductors at room temperature, concerns a different materials capability. Superconducting induction is a measurement tool in the monopole search, and this discovery criterion does not require room-temperature superconductivity. PHY-10, Collider-quality plasma wakefield acceleration, concerns accelerator performance. Improved accelerators could conditionally extend some production searches, but accelerator performance and monopole discovery remain separate achievements.

Scope distinction: emergent monopole-like excitations in materials, including the spin-ice comparison raised in the research, fall outside this free-particle discovery criterion. The supplied evidence does not establish their experimental history, so no claim that spin-ice monopoles have already been observed is adopted here. Their relevance is the distinction between an effective excitation in matter and the free magnetically charged particle targeted by PHY-06.

change_log.change: Preserved PHY-06 and its title while expanding the free-particle and magnetic-charge definition.
change_log.reason: The concept is coherent; limitations in individual supporting assertions do not warrant deleting or redefining it.

change_log.change: Replaced the blanket expectation of extremely heavy, rare monopoles with theory-dependent mass and abundance statements.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports very heavy conventional GUT-scale monopoles, but does not establish a universal abundance prediction.

change_log.change: Replaced the trapped-flux-quantum criterion with a calibrated persistent-current measurement and strengthened the track criterion.
change_log.reason: The reviewed MoEDAL method measures current proportional to magnetic charge; ionization or trapped superconducting flux alone does not establish the target property.

change_log.change: Preserved the 80 GeV and 2–45 Dirac-unit MoEDAL reach while adding its 95% confidence level and production and trapping assumptions.
change_log.reason: The quantitative result is supported within the analysis's scope and should not be generalized into a universal exclusion.

change_log.change: Separated IceCube's previous flux bounds from its developing 2025 analysis and projected sensitivity.
change_log.reason: The quoted 10^-17–10^-18 flux bounds are prior 90% confidence limits that depend on the assumed catalysis cross section.

change_log.change: Retained the reported 2025 MoEDAL and NOvA searches with explicit evidence limitations, and qualified exact publication dates and global discovery status.
change_log.reason: The MoEDAL citation lacks a retained artifact, NOvA lacks a supplied source, and the available search record does not establish coverage through 1 November 2026. These gaps do not prove the reports false.

change_log.change: Separated charge quantization and gauge-structure implications from GUT identification, nucleon-decay catalysis and speculative applications.
change_log.reason: The latter consequences require additional evidence; discovery alone would not establish them.

change_log.change: Removed the universal assertion about isolated magnets and retained the spin-ice comparison only as a scope distinction.
change_log.reason: The supplied review did not document the universal assertion or the claimed observation history of spin-ice monopoles.

change_log.change: Made completion criteria explicitly proposed and explained relevant roster overlaps without merging objectives.
change_log.reason: The suggested demonstrations are not established consensus standards, and related discoveries retain distinct evidentiary requirements.

unresolved_issues: The contents, detailed scope and exact publication date of the cited 2025 MoEDAL full-detector Run 2 paper remain unverified in the supplied review.
The reported 2025 NOvA search has no supplied source, leaving its date, sensitivity, assumptions and outcome unverified here.
The exact 15 August 2024 journal publication date for the beam-pipe paper comes from supplied metadata rather than reviewed document contents.
The supplied record does not establish comprehensive monopole-search or discovery coverage through 1 November 2026.
Monopole masses, cosmic abundance and nucleon-decay catalysis remain theory-dependent; the supplied material does not resolve which scenario, if any, describes nature.
The experimental history of spin-ice monopole-like excitations is not documented by the supplied sources.
